newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index closes at record low.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index closes at record low.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended at a record closing low on Thursday due to heavy overseas liquidation, brokers said.
The index fell 0.226 points or 0.48 percent to 47.077 points, on volume of 8.2 million shares worth $2.9 million, below a record closing low of 47.13 points on June 7 this year.

The market has been in a deep depression, with overseas investors having largely left the market because of continued poor company performance and lack of policy support, with Beijing repeatedly re-affirming a ban on domestic investors trading the foreign currency B shares.
In intra-day trading, the index hit an all-time low of 46.731 points, below the former record low of 47.857 points.
Of 41 B shares, 37 traded, with 17 down, 12 flat and eight up.
Brokers said heavy liquidation of third-tier stock pushed the index down below the 47-point level before support buying brought it back immediately.
"After selling of blue chips in the past few days, third-tier stocks took their turn to fall," one broker said.
"But active support emerged when the index approached its historic low," he added.
"Institutions will fight around 47 points on Friday because market sentiment will worsen if the 47-point level is breached strongly," a second broker said.
Third-tier stocks topped the list of today's falls on institutional liquidation.
Shanghai Steel Tube was the biggest loser, falling $0.010 or 7.69 percent to $0.120, on volume of 188,800 shares.
Shanghai Phoenix Bicycle followed, slipping $0.008 or 6.66 percent to $0.112, on volume of 914,000 shares.
Shanghai Yaohua Pilkington Glass traded the most on intra-institutional trading, ending unchanged at $0.478, on volume of 1.4 million shares.

Shanghai A shares rebounded after yesterday's plunge, but the market is likely to move down to consolidate in the short term, brokers said. The A index rose 19.185 points or 1.90 percent to 1028.536 points, on volume of 593.4 million shares worth 5.6 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index put on 36.581 points or 1.44 percent to 2571.598 points. Beiman Special Steel was the biggest winner, surging 0.65 yuan or 15.11 percent to 4.95 yuan.
